scope: Retrospective user-nominated mechanisms; not random frequencies, a football benchmark, or justification for tuning aggregate numbers. No engine changes.

g1p071.finding: The runner slows under two loaded reaching/diving holds, then regains speed after both slip. Neither first tackler establishes a torso collision; first_contact/hit labels do not establish a body impact.
g1p071.measurement: Exact unrounded body states around World.step; Δp minus recorded external ground impulse gives non-ground body load. No carrier hand constraints or carrier torso contacts occur here, so this diagnoses aggregate grasp transfer. Per-hold vectors are not claimed: reduced supportImpulse bypasses ordinary pairImpulse observer.
g1p071.caveat: Grasp capacities and runner drive have limited measured NFL evidence. This proves load and slowing occur, not that 5.8% speed loss is the correct magnitude. Do not force every broken tackle to lose a fixed percentage of speed.

viewerGeometry.implication: Overlapping enlarged UI markers do not establish body collision. The carrier has zero actual World contact records in this play.

g1p071.playerContextCaution: This runner has breakTackle89 and balance72; the first two defenders both have balance19. Ratings are generated model inputs, not measured NFL quality. Keep these same bodies in comparisons and do not infer population rates from this rep.

nflContactLimits.availableEvidence: BDB2025 first_contact/tackle/ball_snap/handoff events and carrier/defender10Hz positions support contact-relative speed and travel windows. They do not label wrap quality, transmitted grip force, body-surface impact, or why a hold slipped.
nflContactLimits.operatorCaution: On the same1142plays, reported YBC varies from0.372 to0.997yd solely by football-vs-carrier point and metadata-vs-snap LOS. A speed-loss comparison must likewise use identical sampling, rounding, timing and contact definition; labels alone cannot establish physical grip performance.
nflContactLimits.mostUsefulNextComparison: First-contact carrier entry-speed/mass bins with approach angle, nearest-defender geometry, subsequent crowding, first-contact vs tackle interval, and censoring. Independently classify body hit versus reaching contact in film; matching only first_contact mixes very different contacts.

tossVersusOutsideZone.hypothesisSource: User-uploaded12-playfilm review nominated TossG3-P04864yd versus OutsideZoneG4-P074-.74yd. Outcome-selected mechanism contrast, not paired counterfactual, typical frequency or a candidate evaluation.
tossVersusOutsideZone.finding: In the Toss both safeties acquire carrying=true before reaching the runner, but neither establishes a torso hit: two weak reaching/diving holds slip. The FS maintains substantial transverse velocity near the tackle opportunity. In the defensive success, the edge defender closes the body gap and a torso impact sharply slows the runner. This isolates achievable approach/contact geometry before tackle-force calibration.
